item.title: Guided Nature Walk & Ranch House tour Anderson Marsh — Sat Sep 12, 8:30 AM — Anderson Marsh State Historic Park
item.description:
The next “Second Saturday” Guided Nature walk at Anderson Marsh State Historic Park will be held on Saturday, September 12, 2026.
The Guided Walk will begin at 8:30am. Bring binoculars and meet in the parking lot at 8:15am for an opportunity to observe the birds and other wildlife found in the picnic area. Sturdy shoes, a hat and water are suggested.
The September guided walk will be led by State Parks volunteer docent Roberta Lyons and will provide an opportunity to observe wildlife at the park and learn about their natural habitat, as well as to learn about the natural and cultural history of the area.
The walk will take between 1½ and 2 hours, depending on the route taken. Dogs are not allowed on the park trails.
A tour of the historic Anderson Ranch House will be available immediately after the conclusion of the walk.
There is no charge for the Nature Walk and Ranch House tour and parking is free for those attending.
Source: Press Democrat

item.title: Cookbook Club — Sat Sep 12, 12:00 PM — Sonoma Valley Library
item.description: Are you interested in trying new recipes or just wanting to get out of your cooking comfort zone? A cookbook book club blends the joy of reading with the creativity of cooking and the warmth of sharing meals. Browse a selection of themed cookbooks every month, then prepare and share your meals for the next meeting! June: Celebrating Julia in June! Julia Child & Those Influenced by Her. Before "food TV" was a genre, Julia Child was teaching America to cook-joyfully, loudly, and with plenty of permission to make mistakes. Her landmark cookbook Mastering the Art of French Cooking helped translate French technique for American home kitchens launching a whole new way of learning to cook. For this meeting, bring a dish by Julia Child or by chefs influenced by her and who share her spirit-like Jacques Pépin, her longtime cooking partner on public television, and Ina Garten, who has spoken about admiring Child's "courage of her convictions." July: Savoring Summer, Italian-Style. Think Italian

item.description:
Join an immersive, hands-on culinary series at Quivira Vineyards, offered June 7-November 15 from 11 AM - 2 PM. Led by Estate Chef Julia, guests begin in the organic estate garden harvesting seasonal ingredients before moving to the open-air kitchen to prepare a garden-inspired, multi-course meal. This interactive experience highlights the connection between garden, vineyard, and kitchen, while teaching practical culinary techniques. The evening concludes with a shared meal paired with Quivira wines in a beautiful estate setting. Each date features a different focus, including handmade pasta, masa and tacos, stuffed pasta, global dumplings, and seasonal pie baking. Space is limited for these unique seasonal classes.

item.title: FIESTA DE INDEPENDENCIA — Sun Sep 13, 1:00 PM — Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
item.description:
Celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month with a taste of Latin America in Sonoma County! Enjoy authentic food, music, games, and activities for the entire family. Organized by the Center’s Latino Advisory Council, this free, family-friendly, campus-wide festival honors Latin American countries that recognize their independence during this month.
LBC also will present its annual Community Leadership Awards in partnership with Los Cien Sonoma County to an individual and an organization that have demonstrated an outstanding commitment to the Latino Community through volunteerism, education, mentorship, or other personal or professional efforts.
Fiesta de Independencia began at the Center in 2010 to commemorate Mexican Independence Day \(September 16\) and has since evolved to celebrate the rich history of the diverse Latino cultures and people who are an integral part of the North Bay community. Drawing more than 5,000 community members each year, the event has become a Sonoma County tradition

item.description:
This summer, Music in Place and the City of Sonoma invite you to soak up the sunshine, sip local wine, and dance to live music at the Sonoma Plaza Grinstead Amphitheater during Sonoma Sundays On the Plaza, a free concert series running June 7 through October 4, 2026.
Every Sunday from 2:00–5:00 PM, the Plaza comes alive with an exciting mix of musical styles: blues, soul, country, jazz, swing, Americana, mariachi, and more. With a fresh lineup of acclaimed artists, there’s something for everyone to enjoy.
Sonoma Sundays is all about creating opportunities for the community to come together through the power of live music. Music in Place is excited to bring an incredible range of artists to the Plaza this summer and continue building connections through music.
Sonoma Sundays are free and open to all, thanks to the generous support of the Sonoma Community Center, The Dawn Redwoods Trust, and the KHR McNeely Family Foundation.

item.title: Watercolor | Building Technique II, with Nancy Ballard — Tue Sep 15, 10:00 AM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Building on the skills and confidence you developed in the first class, this watercolor workshop invites you to take your ideas a step further. Explore how a simple sketch, thoughtful composition, and expressive use of color can transform an idea into a finished painting.
We'll work larger and bolder while exploring watercolor techniques including:
Wet-on-wet paintingLoose interpretation and expressive mark-makingCreating shadows and depthEnhancing backgroundsWorking in black and whiteExploring the many variations and possibilities of mixing greens
Bring a favorite photograph, a live flower or small plant, or even a meaningful memory to use as inspiration. No matter where you are in your artistic journey, you'll be encouraged to experiment, have fun, and focus on the larger picture rather than striving for perfection. There are no mistakes in art—only opportunities to explore.
Please Note: There will be a $10 supply fee paid directly to the Nancy on the day of the class.

item.title: Stories We Carry — Tue Sep 15, 6:00 PM — Petaluma Historical Library and Museum
item.description:
Every object has a story. Meet the people behind them.
Multiple Dates: September 12 & 19, 6-8 pm
Petaluma Historical Library & Museum
20 4th Street \(Corner of 4th & B Street\)
Free Admission, Light refreshments will be served.
RSVP is recommended.
Join us for two special evenings with the community storytellers featured in Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind. Through family heirlooms, treasured keepsakes, photographs, letters, and everyday belongings, participants will share the deeply personal stories that bring the exhibition to life.
Hear firsthand reflections on migration, identity, resilience, family, and the meaning of home. These intimate conversations offer a rare opportunity to connect directly with the individuals whose voices and objects are featured throughout the exhibition, creating space for dialogue, empathy, and shared understanding.
Following the storytelling program, continue the conversation while exploring the exhibition and enjoying light r

item.title: Introduction to Women's Barbershop Music — Tue Sep 15, 7:00 PM — Finley Person Senior Wing
item.description:
Song of Sonoma is partnering with the Santa Rosa Recreation & Parks Department to present a 1-evening workshop on the American art form of Women’s Barbershop, Tuesday, September 15 from 7:00-9:00.
Women singers of all ages, backgrounds, and abilities will be introduced to the world of barbershop acapella singing. There will be a brief background on what makes barbershop a unique American art form, how it differs from other singing groups, some history, and immersive singing. No experience necessary and the ability to read music is not required.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

item.title: Art Night at Great Company — Thu Sep 17, 5:30 PM — Great Company
item.description:
Join Great Company on Thursday, September 17th for Art Night at 5:30pm. Art night is a free, non-ticketed event, with suggested donations for supplies.
**Art Night** is a monthly gathering focused on community, creativity, and connection.
**Monthly Creative Gathering:** A playful, low-pressure space to create alongside friends and community.
**Project:** We feature 1 new guided art project each month with a short intro and demo to get you started. We always have a library of art supplies available if you’re not feeling the guided project.
**Flexible Supplies:** Use the materials we provide for a **$5–$10 donation\***, or bring your own project to work on for free. *(\*This is all self-funded, so we appreciate any help.)*
**All Skill Levels:** No experience needed! Our roaming hosts are there to offer ideas, tips, and encouragement—it’s about the process, not perfection.
Source: Press Democrat, Visit Santa Rosa
